newsitem.title: ITALY: Coalition parties plan amendments to Italy budget.
newsitem.headline: Coalition parties plan amendments to Italy budget.

text.p: Parties within the government coalition will present a limited number of amendments to the 1997 budget, said Fabio Mussi, the parliamentary leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS).

Among the amendments will be a change to hugely unpopular proposals to hike property taxes, Mussi told reporters after a meeting between other parliamentary leaders from government parties and Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

"We have decided not to present modifications as individual parties but as a single coalition, which will show itself to be strong, water-tight and sufficiently determined to pull-off this budget which will take us into Europe," Mussi said.
The budget, which is designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire from next year's deficit, was unveiled last month and is currently being examined at the commission stage in the lower house of parliament.
Both houses of parliament have until the end of the year to ratify the budget.
"You can count (our) amendments on the fingers of one hand," Mussi said.
The parliamentary party leader of Communist Refoundation, which supports the Prodi government but is not formally a part of the coalition, confirmed his group's backing for the budget.
"Although this is not our budget, because we would have done it differently, we are ready to vote for it with satisfaction," Oliviero Diliberto said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
